problem: If the set $U$ containing all integers is the universal set and $X={0,-1,-2,-3,-4,…}$, then $\overset{―}{X}=$
worked_solution:
The complement of $X,$ denoted $\overset{―}{X},$ consists of every element in the universal set $U$ that is not in the set $X.$

The universal set $U$ consists of the integer numbers while the set $X$ consists of the negative integers and $0.$

So, the only elements of $U$ that are not in $X$ are the natural numbers.

Therefore, the complement of $X$ is

$$
\overset{―}{X}={1,2,3,…}.
$$
